title: Net Resource Allocation: A Desirable Initial Routing Step
problem: Modern IC routing must generate rectilinear Steiner minimum trees (RSMT) for each net and manage limited routing resources among competing nets with inevitable congestion. Current routers address congestion after routing without prior net resource guidance, making it difficult to manage resources efficiently.
motivation: Routing critically impacts chip performance, power, area, and design iteration count, making proactive resource allocation essential for optimizing IC design.
method: The approach introduces Net Region Probability Density (NRPD) to model net resource allocation as a linear programming problem. It solves the LP to obtain posterior NRPD for each net on each grid, then applies a cost scheme based on posterior NRPD and congestion maps to guide routing decisions. The method supports weighted RSMT construction and employs an iterative approach for global routing and track assignment to improve detailed routing quality.
key_novelty: Net Region Probability Density (NRPD)-based linear programming formulation for proactive net resource allocation as an initial routing stage, enabling congestion-aware guidance before detailed routing.
contributions: Introduction of Net Region Probability Density (NRPD) concept for net resource allocation
Linear programming formulation for modeling and solving net resource allocation
Cost scheme leveraging posterior NRPD and congestion maps to guide weighted RSMT construction
Iterative method for global routing and track assignment improving detailed routing quality

metrics.other: routing quality, design rule violations, performance vs OpenROAD
